issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary named in an alternative bequest does not acquire a vested interest where, read with the will as a whole, the bequest is intended to operate only at the testator’s death in specified circumstances.
material_facts: The testator’s will expressed a wish to adopt a boy and authorized his widow to adopt the beneficiary if the testator did not adopt during his lifetime.
One clause provided for the beneficiary’s rights on the footing that he would be adopted by the widow, and directed that arrangements for him be made before the adoption.

A later clause gave the beneficiary and another person equal shares in specified circumstances, including where the testator and his wife died without making an adoption or where the wife predeceased the testator.
The testator died without adopting a boy, his wife survived him, and she did not later adopt the beneficiary.
The beneficiary claimed that, until an adoption occurred, he had a vested interest under the later clause, subject to being divested by a subsequent adoption.
issues.conclusion: The later clause was intended to operate at the testator’s death, not as a continuing bequest pending a possible later adoption. Because the widow survived the testator and no adoption had been made by him, the beneficiary acquired no interest under that clause; his rights under the other clause could arise only if he was adopted by the widow.
issues.legal_principle: A will must be construed as a whole, giving related clauses their plain grammatical meaning considered together. The specific alternative clause was not to be isolated from the provisions concerning adoption. The court applied the approach to will construction stated in Gnanambal Ammal v. T. Raju Ayyar, A.I.R. 1951 S.C. 103, and Venkata Narasimha v. Parthasarathy, L.R. 41 I.A. 51.

rule.if: will_construction_appeal and testator_provided_for_widow_to_adopt_beneficiary and beneficiary_bequest_was_conditioned_on_adoption and no_adoption_by_testator and widow_survived_testator

predicates.will_construction_appeal: A party appealed from a decision construing a will.
predicates.testator_provided_for_widow_to_adopt_ben: The will authorized or directed the testator’s widow to adopt the beneficiary if the testator did not adopt during his lifetime.
predicates.beneficiary_bequest_was_conditioned_on_a: A clause providing for the beneficiary’s rights treated his adoption by the widow as a condition for those rights to arise.
predicates.no_adoption_by_testator: The testator did not adopt a child during his lifetime.
predicates.widow_survived_testator: The testator’s widow was alive when the testator died.

issues.definition: When a will-construction appeal concerns a beneficiary whose rights under the will depend on adoption by a widow, and the testator made no adoption but the widow survived him, the beneficiary has no interest under an alternative bequest construed to operate at the testator’s death.

issues.legal_issue: The principles favoring avoidance of intestacy and immediate vesting are aids to construing a will, not absolute rules that override the testator’s intention expressed by the will as a whole.
material_facts: The beneficiary argued that the will should be construed to avoid intestacy and postponement of vesting.
The court read the relevant clauses together and concluded that the beneficiary’s rights depended on adoption, although this construction allowed for possible intestacy and postponed vesting.
issues.conclusion: The court rejected any presumption that intestacy must be avoided or vesting must not be postponed where the will, construed as a whole, indicates otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: The cardinal task is to ascertain the testator’s intention primarily from the language of the will read as a whole, without conjecture about what the testator might have intended. A presumption against intestacy may be used when the context or circumstances justify it and there is genuine ambiguity, but neither that presumption nor the preference against postponing vesting is absolute. The court relied on Gnanambal Ammal v. T. Raju Ayyar, A.I.R. 1951 S.C. 103, and Venkata Narasimha v. Parthasarathy, L.R. 41 I.A. 51; it distinguished the asserted rules discussed in Sarojini Dassi v. Gnanendranath Das and Bickersteth v. Shanu.

predicates.will_construction_appeal: A party appealed from a decision construing a will.
predicates.will_contains_related_dispositive_clause: The will contains multiple clauses addressing related dispositions or contingencies.
predicates.clauses_can_be_read_together_to_determin: The clauses can be considered together to determine the testator’s intention from the will’s language.

issues.definition: In an appeal construing a will with related clauses that can be read together, preferences against intestacy and postponed vesting do not override the intention shown by the will as a whole.
